correctness.rationale: Exact best replies on positive rival efforts yield F_c. For 4/25<c<1 the map preserves (0,1). The unique Nash point has multiplier -(1-c)^2/(4c), yielding sharp local threshold 3-2sqrt(2). For the subcritical open window F_c^2(y)-y has opposite signs near 0, immediately left/right of Nash, and near 1, forcing a genuine prime-two orbit. At c=1/6 rational outward-square-root intervals establish sign crossing, disjointness and multiplier strictly between 0.17 and 0.18. The supplied executable was run; its exact assertions passed.

originality.rationale: The 2023 primary study presents heterogeneity cycles involving replies to zero and leaves behavior above c=4/25 unresolved analytically. The 2023 convex-cost sequel has a positive-effort cycle for a different nonlinear cost model; the 2024 paper addresses continuous-time and damped dynamics. None of the inspected relevant sections establishes the cost-ratio interval, the Nash multiplier boundary, or the exact interior attracting witness in the linear-cost two-player contest. Classical 1D flip theory alone does not determine the contest-specific invariant interval and existence interval.

value.rationale: The cost ratio 4/25 is an explicit threshold around which the foundational paper reports simulation-based convergence. A rigorous open interval immediately above that bound with nontrivial non-reset cycles and a certified stable rational-cost example addresses a motivated open dynamic question and distinguishes undamped Nash-learning trajectories from equilibria. The sharp multiplier boundary quantifies the loss of local stability; this is not a parameter-renaming or routine table recomputation.
